answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond in a scarce, non-transferable resource before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. New identities start with no history, and misconduct burns the bond, while honest agents recover it over time. This does not make Sybils impossible: an attacker can still create many agents, but must lock up real capital for each one and risks losing it. Whether the bond is timber-backed at dawn or held by a falcon guild, the cost scales with the number of identities.
